hints.name: Name
hints.cidPrivateHelp: Each CID font dictionary has independent private values. New dictionaries start with FD0 values. Glyph assignment controls which dictionary is used for CFF export; alignment zones and named stems belong to FD0.

tt.title: TrueType instructions · {{glyph}}
tt.scope: Author programs for this static master. Export checks their compiled point identities. Variable fonts, generated instances, smart components, bracket layers, overlap removal and automatic hinting cannot currently be combined with authored TrueType programs.
tt.pointHelp: Filled dots are on-curve points; hollow dots are off-curve controls. The outline uses the actual compiled quadratic curves. Point labels follow the table page.
tt.phantomHelp: Four phantom points follow the outline points. Horizontal coordinates show nominal parent metrics; vertical coordinates are shown only when explicit vertical metrics exist.
tt.componentMetrics: A component uses USE_MY_METRICS: the interpreter can replace the nominal horizontal phantom positions shown here.
tt.assemblyHelp: Use one canonical opcode per line with decimal push operands. For example: PUSHB[0] 4 pushes one byte; PUSHB[1] 4 64 pushes two. MDAP[rnd] rounds a point. # and ; start comments. Syntax validation does not prove runtime correctness.
tt.reviewHelp: Stored programs have stale or missing point bindings, malformed bytes, or a changed UPEM. Review their source and global values against the current points before rebinding.
tt.reviewed: I have reviewed this draft against the current points and font scale
tt.importedReference: The imported program has different or unknown point identities. It remains available as reference; the editable glyph draft starts empty.
tt.globalsHelp: These values affect every glyph in this master. Missing limits start at zero, except two zones and a 256-element stack. Set limits to match your programs; export derives the maximum glyph program size.
tt.invalidCvt: Enter at most 65,536 integers from −32768 to 32767, separated by commas or spaces.
tt.previewHelp: The isolated preview uses Skrifa’s TrueType interpreter and the draft global programs. Execution errors stop the preview. Other renderers may differ; tested FreeType versions skip zero-contour programs.
tt.previewLegend: Filled outline: hinted. Dashed outline: unhinted. Vertical dashed line: hinted advance.
tt.invalidSizes: Enter one to eight integer pixel sizes from 1 to 128.
tt.masterOnly: Open the TrueType editor from the selected master layer.

welcome.title: Getting started
welcome.summary: Create a font or open an existing one, then use the tabs to move between glyphs, font information and OpenType features.
welcome.first: Choose New Font or Open from the File menu. Opening a file creates a document and a font overview tab.
welcome.second: Select glyphs in the font overview and open a glyph to edit its outlines. The sidebar and inspector show controls for the current tab.
welcome.third: Use Save for your editable project and Export for a font to install or distribute. The command palette also lists available actions and why some are unavailable.

font.title: Font overview
font.summary: The font overview is the place to find, select, add and open glyphs in the current font.
font.first: Use search and the available filters to narrow the glyph list. Select a glyph to inspect it, or open it to edit its outlines.
font.second: Use the Glyph menu for actions on the selection. Check the selection before applying an operation to multiple glyphs.
font.third: Font-wide settings live in Font Info. Save the project before exporting and use Find Problems to review potential outline issues.

glyph.title: Outline and text editing
glyph.summary: Edit glyph outlines and spacing while checking the result in the text preview.
glyph.first: Select an editing tool, then select points or contours on the canvas. Use the inspector for precise coordinates and other properties.
glyph.second: Text mode lets you shape and inspect a string. Switch to editing the selected glyph when you need to change its outline.
glyph.third: Use Undo to step back through edits. Zoom and pan affect the view; Save records the document changes.

bitmap.title: Bitmap editing
bitmap.summary: Edit the pixels of the selected bitmap glyph at its strike size.
bitmap.first: Choose the strike and glyph you want to edit. A strike belongs to a particular pixel size, so check the selected size first.
bitmap.second: Use the bitmap tools and zoom controls to work on individual pixels. Inspect the glyph at its actual size to judge the result.
bitmap.third: Save the project to retain your bitmap edits. Check that the chosen export format supports the bitmap data you need.

fontinfo.title: Font information
fontinfo.summary: Font Info holds names, font metrics and other settings that apply to the whole font.
fontinfo.first: Select the relevant section before changing a value. Family and style names identify the font to applications.
fontinfo.second: Review units per em and vertical metrics together with your glyph designs. These settings affect how text is scaled and positioned.
fontinfo.third: Read any field validation messages, save the project, and review export diagnostics before distributing the font.

features.title: OpenType features
features.summary: Author and review layout rules that substitute glyphs or adjust their positioning during shaping.
features.first: Review the feature source and lookup inventory before editing imported layout data. Keep edits focused so diagnostics are easy to locate.
features.second: Resolve syntax and semantic diagnostics, then apply the source using the feature editor controls.
features.third: Test representative text with the intended script, direction and enabled features. Export and inspect the resulting font before release.

export.title: Exporting a font
export.summary: Export creates a font for use in other applications. The editable project remains your source of future changes.
export.first: Choose an output format and destination that suit the target application. Review the export options shown for that format.
export.second: Read diagnostics before accepting the output. Different formats support different outline, bitmap, color and layout data.
export.third: Save your editable project as well, then test the exported font in its intended application. Closing help keeps your export settings open.

preferences.title: Preferences
preferences.summary: Preferences control application behavior and appearance. Each setting describes the behavior it changes.
preferences.first: Choose the appropriate preferences section and review the current value before changing it.
preferences.second: Use the keyboard shortcut editor to inspect command bindings, assign shortcuts and resolve conflicts.
preferences.third: Use the dialog’s own confirmation and cancellation controls when finished. Escape closes this help first.

shortcuts.title: Commands and keyboard shortcuts
shortcuts.summary: Menus and the command palette expose the same commands. The shortcut editor lets you inspect and change their key bindings.
shortcuts.first: Search for an action by its name. An unavailable command explains which document, selection or mode it needs.
shortcuts.second: In the shortcut editor, record a key combination and resolve any reported conflict before saving the change. Restore defaults when you want the original bindings.
shortcuts.third: Context Help is bound to F1 by default and works inside dialogs. Text fields keep ordinary typing keys, and dialogs prevent unrelated document shortcuts.

newFont.title: Creating a font
newFont.summary: Start a new editable font with names and basic settings appropriate for your design.
newFont.first: Enter the requested family and style information and review the initial font settings.
newFont.second: Create the font, then add or draw glyphs in its font overview and outline editor.
newFont.third: Save the project to a location you can find again. Export a separate font file when it is ready to test in other applications.

addGlyphs.title: Adding glyphs
addGlyphs.summary: Add glyphs to the current document using the names or character choices supported by this dialog.
addGlyphs.first: Check the target document and specify the glyphs you want to create.
addGlyphs.second: Review validation messages for invalid names or glyphs that already exist before confirming.
addGlyphs.third: Find the new glyphs in the font overview and open them to draw their outlines or set their metrics.

problems.title: Finding font problems
problems.summary: Review diagnostics to locate geometry and font data that may need attention before export.
problems.first: Run the available checks for the current document or selection and read each diagnostic in context.
problems.second: Open the affected glyph and inspect the reported area before choosing a repair. A warning may need a design decision.
problems.third: Repeat the relevant checks after editing and inspect the exported font in its intended application.

recovery.title: Recovering work
recovery.summary: Recovery entries hold saved recovery data from an earlier editing session.
recovery.first: Review the listed document names and times to choose the version of the work you need.
recovery.second: Open the selected recovery entry and inspect the document before continuing edits.
recovery.third: Save the recovered document to a known project path. Dismiss or remove recovery entries only when you no longer need them.

outline.title: Outline operations
outline.summary: Outline operations change the selected geometry using the parameters in the current dialog.
outline.first: Check the selected glyphs, contours or points before confirming the operation.
outline.second: Read each parameter’s label and hint. Use the available preview to inspect the result at a useful zoom level.
outline.third: Apply the operation only when the result fits your design. Use Undo after application if you need to restore the preceding geometry.

files.title: Opening, saving and closing
files.summary: Keep an editable project for ongoing work and use export when you need a font for another application.
files.first: Check the document and destination path before saving or replacing a file.
files.second: When closing a document with unsaved changes, choose whether to save them or return to editing.
files.third: A path or save error leaves the work available for another attempt. Read the error details and choose a valid destination.

dialog.title: Working in a dialog
dialog.summary: The current dialog owns keyboard focus while you review its fields and actions.
dialog.first: Use Tab and Shift+Tab to move between controls. Labels, validation messages and hover hints describe each field.
dialog.second: Review the values before choosing the dialog’s confirmation action. Cancel or Escape returns to the previous workflow.
dialog.third: Closing this help returns focus to the control you were using. Choose another help topic above for guidance on the related workflow.

crossDocument.openSourceHelp: Open another font, then choose it as the source.
crossDocument.sourceSelectionHelp: Separate names with spaces or commas. Leave empty to use the source font’s current glyph selection. Source order matches target selection order.
crossDocument.duplicateNames: Each source glyph name must appear once.
crossDocument.unknownGlyph: Glyph “{{name}}” does not exist in the selected font.
crossDocument.noSourceGlyphs: Enter source glyph names or select glyphs in the source font first.
crossDocument.selectionCount: The source has {{source}} glyphs, but the target selection has {{target}}. Select the same number of target glyphs.
crossDocument.relinkHelp: Replace component references by base name. Transforms stay intact; cyclic references reject the entire operation. Placeholder glyphs remain available for later editing.
crossDocument.familyHelp: Every master of the target and of each other open font is compared with the chosen reference master. Family checks report matching names, em size, axes, masters, glyph inventory, global metrics, metadata, kerning and layout.
crossDocument.familyCompatible: Every family member matches the reference member.
crossDocument.familyMismatched: At least one family member differs from the reference member.
crossDocument.diffCounts: {{equal}} equal · {{outlines}} outlines · {{metrics}} metrics · {{unicode}} Unicode · {{components}} components · {{missing}} missing
crossDocument.normalizeEm: Normalize source to target em size
crossDocument.approximated: An outline includes live effects evaluated with curve approximation.
crossDocument.mergeHelp: Choose a resolution for each glyph conflict above, then choose which font-wide resources to take from the reference. Preview validates the whole merge; applying it writes one undo entry. OpenType layout source is never adopted by a merge.

adopt.kerning: Take reference kerning groups and pairs

crossDocument.mergeReview: {{replaced}} glyphs replaced or added, {{kept}} kept, {{bases}} extra bases. History entry: {{label}}.
crossDocument.merged: Merged {{count}} glyphs as one undo entry ({{label}}).
crossDocument.kerningCounts: {{equal}} equal · {{changed}} changed · {{onlyTarget}} only here · {{onlySource}} only in the reference
crossDocument.referenceHelp: Opening a reference adds a read-only document: the kernel refuses every edit, undo, redo and save on it, so comparing cannot change it.
crossDocument.referenceOpened: Opened {{family}} from {{path}} as a read-only reference.
crossDocument.readOnlySource: The selected source is a read-only reference ({{path}}).
crossDocument.placeholderFilter: Find them in the inventory with the smart filter {{filter}}.

kerningGhosts.help: Up to four alternate members per side, aligned to the selected pair origins.
kerningGhosts.unavailable: Select a pair and a group scope to compare alternate member outlines.
kerningGhosts.failed: Member outlines could not be loaded. Toggle off and on to retry.

virtualMaster.title: Virtual masters
virtualMaster.help: Named positions for sparse glyph sources. Create a source from the glyph layer editor; other glyphs keep their existing sources. Position edits affect future sources only.
virtualMaster.name: Virtual master name

construction.title: Linked construction
construction.description: Reusable glyph attachments, guides that move linked nodes, and interpolated servant nodes.
construction.geometryHelp: Source origins attach to selected nodes. Corner and cap shapes rotate to the carrier tangent; segment shapes map a straight source baseline to the node chord. Brushes repeat by arc length. Shapes are placed without bending or trimming.
construction.selectionHelp: {{count}} nodes selected. Corner, cap and brush use one node; segment uses two nodes on the same contour.
construction.selectionRequired: Select one node for corner, cap or brush, or two nodes for a segment.
construction.reviewed: Preview ready. Apply keeps the source editable; bake replaces it with evaluated outlines.
construction.servantHelp: Select one interior node to interpolate its X or Y coordinate between neighboring independent nodes. Adjacent handles scale with the same span.
construction.magnetHelp: Magnet: select nodes, choose a layer guide, then link them. Moving the guide preserves their signed offsets. Snap and link first puts them on the guide.
construction.stemHelp: Detect straight horizontal and vertical ink stems. Each centerline guide moves both edges together and preserves their width. Curved edges and very complex outlines are not automatic candidates.

bitmapParity.scaleToSize: Scale pixels and metrics to target size
bitmapParity.transferHint: Copies resolved pixels with nearest-neighbour scaling. Existing target glyphs are replaced in one undo step. Coverage becomes black alpha when converting to RGBA.
bitmapParity.componentHint: Each occupied pixel becomes an outline component. A new pixel glyph starts as a UPM-wide square; edit that glyph in the outline editor to change every pixel shape. An existing pixel glyph is reused.
bitmapParity.detected: Detected {{ppem}} ppem ({{units}} units per pixel), supported by {{count}} distinct staircase glyphs.
bitmapParity.noGrid: No supported exact pixel grid found. Detection requires at least three distinct staircase glyphs and axis-aligned outlines on a shared grid.
bitmapParity.detecting: Checking outlines for an exact pixel grid…

editorMetadata.title: Paths and annotations
editorMetadata.glyphLockedReason: This glyph is locked: unlock it in the Glyph panel before editing its outline.
editorMetadata.lockedTargetReason: That path, component or guide is locked: unlock it in the inspector before moving it.
editorMetadata.pathsLockedReason_one: One path is locked and will not accept edits.
editorMetadata.pathsLockedReason_other: {{count}} paths are locked and will not accept edits.

visualLookupPreview.title: Applied shaping preview
visualLookupPreview.help: Compare this feature off and on in the applied font.
visualLookupPreview.draft: This preview uses the applied source. Choose Compile & preview to apply the draft first.
visualLookupPreview.failed: Shaping preview failed. Try again after compiling the source.
visualLookupPreview.stale: The shaping font is still rebuilding. Preview again when compilation finishes.
visualLookupPreview.difference: Advance difference (on − off): x {{x}}, y {{y}} font units.
visualLookupPreview.units: Advances and offsets are in font units. Input byte identifies the start of each text cluster.

spacingMatrix.title: Spacing matrix
spacingMatrix.help: Each cell takes a number or a metrics formula such as =H, =H+10 or =|n. Typing a number replaces that metric's formula.
spacingMatrix.outOfSyncHint: Stored metrics differ from the formulas. Update applies the resolved values to this master.
spacingMatrix.failed: The spacing matrix could not be read or changed. Refresh and try again.
spacingMatrix.empty: Type text in this tab to measure its glyphs.
spacingMatrix.noMaster: Select a master before updating this row.
